Layer-23 MLP loop neurons: add a rank-1 push along the layer-23 commit direction d (commit-vs-loop mean-difference of hidden_23; cosine 0.96 with the within-problem version) to the down_proj columns of the 13 neurons that fire specifically in looping traces (tail 0.3-2.2 vs head ~0, pre-commit <0.26, consistent across 12 distinct problems). Scaling a_j/S makes the push equal 1.2 hidden units when those neurons fire at their loop rate, ~1/3 of the measured 3.65-unit loop->commit gap, while neurons silent outside loops add nothing, so ordinary reasoning is untouched. Evidence: 96.9% of failures are non-terminating thinking, 50% of cut traces already contain the gold answer, and along the commit direction the looping state sits at -2.83 vs +0.82 at successful </think>.

Layer-23 loop-neuron close gate: for the 13 MLP neurons that fire specifically in looping thinking (gate sum 20.2 in loop tails vs 4.8 at trace heads and 4.6 in ordinary reasoning), add lam*ueff*Aend[j]/S to down_proj column j with lam=0.20, ueff = final-RMSNorm-weighted read-out direction of '</think>' (norm_w*w_close; 26.8 logits per hidden unit at ||h||=2.3) and Aend the neurons' mean activation at line ends of looping traces. Evidence: 96.9% of failures never close thinking; after a loop's blank line even 'Ready' is at -21.7 logits, so no commitment phrase can start, while '</think>' costs only -0.56 once a phrase exists - the missing signal is the close token itself, and the push supplies ~5.4 logits where the loop detector fires (1.4 at head/commit-region gate levels) without touching the other 3571 neurons.

Layer-23 loop-gated close read-out: add a rank-1 push along the final-norm-weighted </think> embedding direction to the down_proj columns, gated by a diagonal LDA direction on layer-23 MLP activations that is positive in looping thinking (mean 1.0 at the true close position of 48 real failing traces) and near zero for successful traces (mean -0.07) and mid-reasoning. alpha=0.4 adds 0.77 hidden units at loop close positions, enough to raise </think> by several nats, while off-loop positions receive ~0. The earlier layer-23 edit was invalid because it was tested on a duplicated </think>; this one is built from the clean pass 15 close positions.

Loop-gated close read-out at doubled strength: layer-23 down_proj gets W + 0.8*u*g^T, where u is the final-norm-weighted </think> embedding and g is the layer-23 MLP loop gate. The alpha=0.4 version raised the true close log-probability by 5.74 nats on 48/48 real loop prefixes while changing successful prefixes by -0.45, but left it at -4.4, too low to sample; alpha=0.8 targets the remaining gap. The gate is near zero for successful and mid-reasoning traces (mean -0.05 at success close positions), so ordinary reasoning is not globally sharpened.

Layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out at half strength. The alpha=0.8 version gave a paired +8.98pp (se 2.03, 26 rescues vs 3 losses) but 192/256 samples ran away: median first close at ~956 chars, then a median of 7,731 repeated </think> tokens instead of an answer, because the close logit was pushed to ~0 at every loop position (alpha=0.8: mean close lp -1.66, median -0.12). Alpha=0.4 measured mean close lp -4.41 (still +5.74 nats over the -10.15 baseline, 48/48 loop prefixes improved) while successful close positions stay at -11.1, so the close becomes reachable without dominating the next-token distribution.

Layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out at alpha=0.2. Paired generation showed a monotone dose-response downward: alpha=0.8 gave +8.98pp (se 2.03) but 192/256 samples degenerated into thousands of repeated </think> tokens; alpha=0.4 gave +25.78pp (se 2.90, 69 rescues vs 3 losses) and cut share fell 90.6%->53.9%, with only 22 wrong finished answers. Since the weaker push is better and half of 0.4-samples still exhaust the budget, alpha=0.2 keeps the close reachable exactly in looping states (uniformly scaled-down version of the same gated read-out) while reducing the chance of an early close and of the close-token attractor.

Layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out at alpha=0.5. Paired dose-response on the same 64 problems x4 is peaked: alpha=0.2 -> +10.16pp (se 2.46, 34 rescues/8 losses), alpha=0.4 -> +25.78pp (se 2.90, 69 rescues/3 losses, cut share 90.6%->53.9%), alpha=0.8 -> +8.98pp (se 2.03) with </think>-repetition runaways. 0.5 sits just above the current best, to locate the optimum: it is the same gated close read-out, only stronger than 0.4.

Restore the best measured strength of the layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out (alpha=0.4). Paired dose-response on identical 64 problems x4: 0.2 -> +10.16pp (se 2.46), 0.4 -> +25.78pp (se 2.90, 69 rescues/3 losses), 0.5 -> +25.00pp (se 2.93), 0.8 -> +8.98pp with </think>-spam runaways. 0.4 and 0.5 tie on accuracy but 0.4 leaves far fewer finished-wrong or no-answer samples (23 vs 44), so 0.4 is the safer point on the plateau. The edit pushes the final-norm-weighted </think> direction, gated by a diagonal-LDA detector on layer-23 MLP activations that is positive in looping thinking, making the close token reachable exactly where thinking has stalled (close lp -10.15 -> -4.41 on 48/48 loop prefixes).

Layer-23 loop-gated close read-out, end-of-turn leak removed. Same structure as the validated alpha=0.4 edit (W0 + 0.4*u*g^T, g = layer-23 MLP loop gate), but u is now orthogonalised against the final-norm-weighted <|im_end|> and <|endoftext|> output rows (2x2 Gram projection). Weight analysis: the old u gave </think> +1.02 logits/unit but also <|im_end|> +0.23 (z=6.5) and <|endoftext|> +0.18 (z=4.9) per unit, and the gate is highest exactly where the answer stage dies (mean gate 1.29 at the final position of the 40 no-answer traces vs 0.36 in healthy answer regions), so in a stuck trace the edit pushed end-of-turn immediately after </think>: 11 of 40 no-answer traces at 32k stop with a zero-length answer region and the median dying answer region is only 119 chars. The new u keeps 95% of its </think> coefficient (+0.975) while zeroing both end-of-turn coefficients, so the close stays reachable in loops but no longer drags the model out of the answer stage.

Post-commit switch-off for the layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out (same alpha=0.4 and same read-out direction u2 as the validated edit; only the gate changes). Dense measurement on real traces: the gate averages 2.12 at the first (needed) close of the 45 spam cuts but still 0.92 at the spurious post-commit closes inside answer regions, where </think> has no <|im_end|> in the top-10 and the 1.5 presence penalty cannot stop it - that is the 45-cut bucket in the 256-problem confirmation (54.7% vs 9.8%). The post-minus-pre mean-difference direction dhat of the layer-23 MLP inputs (orthogonalised to the pre-commit mean, projection 6.6 post vs 0.0 pre) is subtracted at lambda=0.12, giving gate mean 2.12->2.12 at pre-commit closes (93% still >1) and 0.92->0.25 at spurious post-commit positions. The read-out therefore still fires exactly when thinking has stalled but stops re-closing inside the answer stage.

Composite answer-stage switch-off for the layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out (same u2, same alpha=0.4). The measured 256-problem result of the first switch-off was 57.8% vs 10.2% (+47.7pp, se 3.2) with cuts 45->32 and noans 22->14; the 32 remaining cuts still re-close </think> deep in the answer region. Gate statistics from 60k real layer-23 MLP inputs: the old term g-0.12*dhat gives answer-region gate 0.11 but leaves scattered firing; the added whitened direction w (fit so w.x=0 on pre-commit thinking and w.x=1 on answer-region activations; pre-commit unchanged 1.873->1.858 with 85% still >1, while near/far answer positions go to -1.17/-0.70 and the observed spurious closes to -0.19). Thus the close stays reachable exactly where thinking has stalled but cannot re-fire once the answer stage has begun.

Revert the failed added answer-region suppression w (edit #50). Paired 256-problem generation with #50 was 52.34% vs original 9.77% (+42.58pp, se 3.24), while the previous #49 u2+0.12*dhat version on the same held-out items was 57.81% vs 10.16% (+47.66pp, se 3.18). The w term converted ~14 correct answers into 10 extra wrong and 6 extra cut traces, so the measured-best #49 read-out is restored.

Stronger post-commit switch-off for the validated layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out. Same u2 read-out and alpha=0.4 as the measured-best edit (#49: 57.81% vs orig 10.16% on 256 held-out problems, +47.66pp se 3.18); only the suppression of the post-commit gate term rises from 0.12 to 0.24 along dhat, the post-minus-pre mean-difference direction of layer-23 MLP inputs that is orthogonalised to the pre-commit mean. Evidence: #49 cut the re-firing cuts 45->32 and answer deaths 22->14 relative to no suppression, but 32 traces still lock into the close token (median 9,641 </think> emissions, first close at median relative position 0.16, zero boxed answers), i.e. the gate still fires inside/after the answer stage; doubling the orthogonal dhat term lowers that stage's gate further while leaving the pre-commit gate untouched by construction.

Restore the measured-best layer-23 loop-gated close read-out (#49): W0 + 0.4*u2*g^T with g = g_lda - 0.12*dhat. Paired 256-problem evaluation on identical held-out items: #49 gave 57.81% vs 10.16% (+47.66pp se 3.18); the same edit with the post-commit coupling raised to 0.24 gave 51.95% vs 7.81% (+44.14pp se 3.21) with cuts 32->38, so the stronger coupling has no support and the validated 0.12 strength is restored.

Second, post-commit-gated rank-1 term on the layer-23 down_proj: add beta*n_hat*g_post^T on top of the validated close read-out (#49). n_hat is the final-norm-weighted newline read-out orthogonalised to </think>, <|im_end|> and <|endoftext|> (so it cannot re-trigger a close or end the turn) and g_post = dhat/6.59 is the post-minus-pre mean-difference detector of layer-23 MLP inputs, whose projection is 6.59 at post-commit closes and 0.00 at pre-commit closes. beta is set so a typical post-commit position gains ~3 nats on the answer-start newline, comparable to the ~5 nats the close push still contributes there. Evidence: with #49 alone 34/256 traces close </think> early (first close at median relative position 0.16), emit no \boxed at all and then repeat </think> thousands of times; the fixed presence penalty is only -1.5 nats, so nothing breaks the tie in favour of starting the answer. This term provides the missing answer-start push exactly after a close and near zero before it.

Layer-23 post-commit \boxed read-out, added on top of the validated #49 close read-out (W = W49 + gamma*b_hat*g_post^T). b_hat is the final-norm-weighted read-out of the \boxed token orthogonalised to </think>, <|im_end|> and <|endoftext|> (so it cannot re-close thinking or end the turn); g_post = dhat/6.59 is the post-minus-pre mean-difference detector of layer-23 MLP inputs with projection 6.59 at post-commit positions and 0.00 at pre-commit closes, so the term is inactive while thinking is still running. gamma gives 2.5 nats on \boxed at g_post=1. Evidence: with #49 alone the residual buckets on both the confirmation set and the fresh set are ~16 finished traces that write a complete plain answer ('Thus, the time is 0.') but never emit \boxed, and are therefore ungraded; a previous attempt that pushed the generic newline token instead produced whitespace loops (98% cuts), so this term uses the single task-specific answer token, which cannot self-reinforce into whitespace.

Weaker-strength version (alpha=0.3) of the validated layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out, testing the strength at the deployment length. Same u2 read-out (final-norm-weighted </think> orthogonalised to <|im_end|>/<|endoftext|>) and same gate (diagonal-LDA loop detector minus 0.12*post-commit direction); only alpha drops from 0.4 to 0.3. Evidence: alpha=0.4 measured 57.8% vs 10.2% on 256 held-out problems at 32k and 57.8% vs 9.8% on a fresh 256-problem set (+48.1pp, se 3.2), but its residual failures are 32-34 traces whose FIRST </think> arrives at median relative position 0.16, i.e. premature closes that then spam the close token; the strength was originally selected at an 8k cap where every extra closed trace is immediately graded, so a weaker push at 32k should keep the close reachable in genuine stalls while making those premature closes less likely.

Strength test at alpha=0.5 for the validated layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out (same u2 final-norm-weighted close direction, same g = diagonal-LDA loop detector minus 0.12*post-commit direction). Evidence: on the same 256-problem confirmation set at the deployment length of 32,768 tokens, alpha=0.3 produced 96 close-spam cuts and 129 correct, alpha=0.4 produced 32 cuts and 148 correct (57.8%), so the number of traces locked in the close token falls steeply as the push grows and 0.4 is not past the optimum; an earlier 8k-capped dose-response had 0.5 essentially tied with 0.4 (+25.0 vs +25.8pp), so 0.5 is the natural next point to test at 32k, where extra room lets a closed trace still reach its answer.

Restore the fully validated layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out (#49: W0 + 0.4*u2*g^T, g = g_lda - 0.12*dhat). Strength dose-response measured at the deployment length of 32,768 tokens on the same 256 held-out problems: alpha 0.3 -> 50.4% (96 close-spam cuts), alpha 0.4 -> 57.8% (32 cuts), alpha 0.5 -> 46.5% (70 cuts); post-commit coupling 0 -> 54.7%, 0.12 -> 57.8%, 0.24 -> 52.0%. alpha=0.4 with lambda=0.12 is the measured optimum and was independently confirmed on a fresh, never-used 256-problem set at 57.8% vs 9.8% (+48.1pp, se 3.2). Alternative second read-out terms (whitened answer-region suppression, newline push, \boxed push) were all measured and were harmful, so this tensor is the best evidenced version.

Second rank-1 term on the layer-23 down_proj, added to the validated close read-out (#49): W = W49 + 3.0*b_hat*w_end^T. w_end is a ridge-LDA direction on layer-23 MLP inputs fitted to fire at the end-of-turn state: it projects +0.645 (q10 +0.552) at the 22 no-answer traces' end positions where <|im_end|> is predicted, versus +0.018 (q99 +0.080) over 2,927 ordinary thinking positions, and it is nearly orthogonal to both the loop gate (-0.03) and the post-commit direction (+0.013). b_hat is the final-norm-weighted read-out of the \boxed token orthogonalised to </think>, <|im_end|> and <|endoftext|>, so it can neither re-close thinking nor end the turn. Evidence: with #49 alone the residual failures include 14-22 traces that write a complete plain answer and then stop at end-of-turn without ever emitting \boxed, and are therefore ungraded; a previous \boxed push failed because its gate (the post-commit direction) was large in ordinary answer text, while this gate is silent in thinking and fires only at the end-of-turn state.

Restore the measured-best layer-23 loop-gated </think> read-out (#49) after the failed end-of-turn \boxed push. Paired 256-problem generation on identical held-out items: the \boxed term scored 53.52% while #49 scored 57.81%; per-sample transitions were 25 correct->wrong, 12 correct->cut and only 14 wrong->correct, and traces containing \boxed fell from 211 to 199. The end-of-turn gate's leave-one-window-out separation was +0.07 against an ordinary-position 99th percentile of 0.08, so it fired inside the answer region and derailed answers instead of making the box reachable. #49 is the best measured configuration and is restored bit-exactly.
